extracted.intended_audience: attorneys, registered practitioners, respondents, OED staff, and hearing officers involved in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and substantive procedural standards governing investigations, disciplinary proceedings, hearings, evidentiary practice, sanctions, appeals, and reinstatement for practitioners before the USPTO (Office of Enrollment and Discipline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney representation and declaration (§11.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual respondent may represent themself or be represented by an attorney before the Office in connection with an investigation or disciplinary proceeding. The attorney shall file a written declaration that he or she is an attorney within the meaning of § 11.1 and shall state the address to which the attorney wants correspondence related to the investigation or disciplinary proceeding sent, and a telephone number where the attorney may be reached during normal business hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The declaration must include the correspondence address and daytime telephone number; this information is used for service and contact during the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counsel for OED Director must be screened from certain consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorneys in the Office of the Solicitor representing the OED Director shall not consult with the USPTO Director, the General Counsel, the Deputy General Counsel for General Law, or an individual designated by the USPTO Director to decide disciplinary matters regarding the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This isolation is intended to prevent conflicts and preserve impartial decision-making; the rule was added/updated by notice references.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Counsel and Deputy General Counsel screening
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Counsel and the Deputy General Counsel for General Law shall remain screened from the investigation and prosecution of all disciplinary proceedings in order that they shall be available as counsel to the USPTO Director in deciding disciplinary proceedings unless access is appropriate to perform their duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They may be made available after final decision to counsel the USPTO Director as needed; screening preserves availability as decision counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing location and definition of 'filed' (§11.41)
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers filed after the complaint and prior to entry of an initial decision by the hearing officer shall be filed with the hearing officer at an address or place designated by the hearing officer. The term 'filed' means the delivery, mailing, or electronic transmission of a document to a hearing officer or designee in connection with a disciplinary complaint or related matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After entry of an initial decision, papers must be filed with the USPTO Director and a copy served on the OED Director. The hearing officer or OED Director may prescribe filing by hand, Priority Mail Express®, or other means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of papers on represented respondents (§11.42(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers other than a complaint shall be served on a respondent who is represented by an attorney by (1) delivering a copy to the office of the attorney; (2) mailing by first-class mail, Priority Mail Express®, or other delivery service to the attorney at the address provided under § 11.40(a)(1); or (3) any other method mutually agreeable to the attorney and a representative for the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the attorney's declared address; parties may agree to other methods of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of papers on unrepresented respondents (§11.42(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers other than a complaint shall be served on a respondent who is not represented by an attorney by (1) delivering a copy to the respondent; (2) mailing by first-class mail, Priority Mail Express®, or other delivery service to the respondent at the address to which a complaint may be served or such other address as designated in writing by the respondent; or (3) any other method mutually agreeable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When unrepresented, use the complaint service address or other written address provided by respondent; parties can agree to alternative service methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service on OED representative and certificate of service (§11.42(c)-(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent shall serve on the representative for the OED Director one copy of each paper filed with the hearing officer or the OED Director by delivery, mailing to an address designated by the representative, or any mutually agreeable method. Each paper filed must contain a certificate of service indicating the date and method of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates of service must show date and method; failure to include may affect proof of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing officer may require specified service methods; service by mail completed on USPS custody (§11.42(e)-(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing officer or the USPTO Director may require that a paper be served by hand or by Priority Mail Express®. Service by mail is completed when the paper mailed in the United States is placed into the custody of the U.S. Postal Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict rules on completion of mail service remove disputes about when service occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions content, format, and conferral requirement (§11.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions, including prehearing motions commonly filed under the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, shall be served on the opposing party and filed with the hearing officer. Each motion shall set forth a basis for the requested relief, including a concise statement of the facts and supporting reasons, along with a citation of the authorities upon which the movant relies. For motions for summary judgment or to dismiss, the basis shall be provided in a written memorandum. All motions and accompanying memoranda shall be double-spaced and written in 12-point font unless otherwise ordered by the hearing officer. Every motion must include a statement that the moving party or attorney has conferred with the opposing party in a good-faith effort to resolve the issues and whether the motion is opposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions must be substantive (facts, reasons, authorities), comply with formatting, and include a good-faith conferral statement; failure to confer or include required content may result in denial or refusal to consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions response and reply deadlines (§11.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the hearing officer extends the time for good cause, the opposing party shall serve and file a memorandum in response to any motion for summary judgment or motion to dismiss within 21 days of service of the motion, and the moving party may file a reply memorandum within 14 days after service of the opposing party's responsive memorandum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines are default and may be extended for good cause by the hearing officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing administration and recording (§11.44(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing officer shall preside over hearings. After the time for filing an answer has elapsed, the hearing officer shall set the time and place for the hearing. The hearing officer may order a hearing to be conducted by remote videoconference in whole or in part. Oral hearings will be recorded and transcribed, testimony of witnesses received under oath or affirmation, and the hearing officer shall conduct the hearing as if the proceeding were subject to 5 U.S.C. 556. A copy of the transcript becomes part of the record and will be provided to the OED Director and the respondent at the expense of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing procedures conform to administrative hearing norms; remote hearings permitted; transcripts are official record material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of respondent failing to appear (§11.44(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to appear after a notice of hearing, the hearing officer may deem the respondent to have waived the opportunity for a hearing and may proceed in the absence of the respondent. The hearing officer may strike the answer or any other pleading, deem the respondent to have admitted the facts alleged in the complaint, receive evidence in aggravation or mitigation, enter a default judgment, and/or enter an initial decision imposing discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to appear can result in severe procedural consequences including default judgment and imposition of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to hearings and protective orders (§11.44(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A hearing will not be open to the public except that the hearing officer may grant a request by a respondent to open the hearing to the public and make the record available for public inspection, provided a protective order is entered to exclude from public disclosure information privileged or confidential under applicable laws or regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public access is the exception and is conditioned on protective orders to safeguard privileged/confidential information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of pleadings (§11.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may, without Committee on Discipline authorization but with the authorization of the hearing officer, amend the complaint to include additional charges based upon conduct committed before or after the complaint was filed. If amendment is authorized, the hearing officer shall authorize amendment of the answer. Any party prejudiced by the amendment will be given reasonable opportunity to meet the allegations and the hearing officer shall make findings on any issue presented by the complaint or answer as amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are permitted by OED with hearing officer approval and require reasonable opportunity for parties to respond; hearing officer must resolve issues raised by amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof standard (§11.49)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a disciplinary proceeding, the OED Director shall have the burden of proving the violation by clear and convincing evidence and a respondent shall have the burden of proving any affirmative defense by clear and convincing evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the government's case and any affirmative defenses are measured by the clear and convincing evidence standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary rule: admissibility and exclusions (§11.50(a),(b),(c),(d),(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules of evidence prevailing in courts are not controlling, but the hearing officer shall exclude evidence that is irrelevant, immaterial, speculative, or unduly repetitious. Depositions taken pursuant to § 11.51 may be admitted. Official documents, records, and papers of the Office are admissible without extrinsic evidence of authenticity and may be evidenced by a copy certified as correct by an employee. Exhibits introduced may be withdrawn subject to conditions. Objections to evidence will be in short form stating the grounds; objections and rulings are part of the record and no exception is necessary to preserve rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flexible evidentiary approach but with exclusions for irrelevance/speculation/repetition; government records have presumptive admissibility; objections are summarized in short form and need not be preserved by exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions: authorization, notice, and limits (§11.51)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositions in lieu of personal appearance may be taken by respondent or OED by agreement or upon a showing of good cause and with hearing officer approval; if granted, a subpoena will be authorized under 35 U.S.C. 24. Notice of deposition must be reasonable (not less than 14 days unless shortened by agreement or hearing officer). Depositions may be oral or by written questions before an authorized officer; deposition expenses are borne by the party requesting the deposition. When taken on written questions, written questions and any cross-questions have service timing rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositions are discretionary and subject to notice and procedural safeguards; parties bear their own costs for depositions they seek.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on taking depositions for discovery (§11.51(g)-(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositions may not be taken to obtain discovery except as provided; when OED and respondent agree in writing, a discovery deposition of any witness who will appear voluntarily may be taken under mutually agreeable terms. Discovery depositions shall not be filed with the hearing officer and may not be admitted into evidence unless the hearing officer orders admission; admissibility is within the hearing officer's discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery via depositions is strictly limited and requires either agreement or hearing officer authorization; the hearing officer may refuse to admit discovery depositions into evidence for reasonable bases (demeanor, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written discovery authorization and scope (§11.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: After an answer is filed, a party may file a motion seeking authorization to propound written discovery of relevant evidence, including a reasonable number of requests for admission (including genuineness of documents), interrogatories, documents to be produced, and other things for inspection and copying. The motion must include proposed requests and explain how each is reasonable and relevant to an issue actually raised in the complaint or answer. Responses must include specific objections; objections not raised are deemed waived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery is permission-based; the moving party must justify each request's relevance and reasonableness in the motion; specificity in objections is required or they'll be waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited discovery subjects (§11.52(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery shall not be authorized of any matter that: (1) will be used solely for impeachment; (2) is not available under 35 U.S.C. 122; (3) relates to any other disciplinary proceeding before the Office; (4) relates to experts; (5) is privileged; or (6) relates to mental impressions, conclusions, opinions, or legal theories of any attorney or other representative of a party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories protect privileged, irrelevant, duplicative, or internal deliberative materials from discovery in disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for denying discovery (§11.52(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing officer may deny discovery if it will unduly delay the proceeding, place an undue burden on the producing party, or consists of information that is available generally to the public, equally to the parties, or to the requesting party through another source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery is discretionary and may be denied to prevent delay, undue burden, or duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for admission deemed admitted if not answered (§11.52(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for admission will be deemed admitted if the party to whom the request is directed fails to respond or object within the time allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely responses to requests for admission are essential to avoid automatic admissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-hearing statement requirements (§11.52(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing officer may require parties to file and serve, prior to any hearing, a pre-hearing statement containing: (1) a list and copies of all proposed exhibits; (2) a list of proposed witnesses; (3) for each proposed expert witness, identification of field, subject matter expected to testify about, and a complete statement of all opinions expected and the basis and reasons for them; and (4) copies of memoranda reflecting respondent's own statements to administrative representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-hearing statements promote orderly presentation and provide notice of exhibits, witness testimony, and expert opinions; failure to include required information may result in exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-hearing memoranda and page/time limits (§11.53)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in default circumstances, the hearing officer shall afford parties a reasonable opportunity to submit proposed findings and conclusions and a post-hearing memorandum. The OED Director must serve and file a post-hearing memorandum within 30 days after the transcript is filed; the respondent has 30 days after service to file a responsive post-hearing memorandum. The OED Director may reply within 21 days after service of any responsive memorandum. Post-hearing memoranda and responsive memoranda shall be limited to 50 pages (12-point font, double-spaced, one-inch margins), and reply memoranda limited to 25 pages, unless otherwise ordered. The hearing officer may extend time and increase page limits for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the specified deadlines and strict page/format limits unless the hearing officer grants relief for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of initial decision (§11.55(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing officer shall make an initial decision that includes: (1) a statement of findings of fact and conclusions of law, and the reasons or bases for those findings and conclusions with specific references to the record upon all material issues presented; and (2) an order of default judgment, suspension or exclusion from practice, reprimand, probation, or dismissal of the complaint, and may impose any conditions deemed appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initial decision must explain factual and legal conclusions with record citations and specify any disciplinary order or conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to consider in determining sanctions (§11.55(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining any sanction, the following factors shall be considered if applicable: (1) whether the practitioner violated a duty owed to a client, the public, the legal system, or the profession; (2) whether the practitioner acted intentionally, knowingly, or negligently; (3) the amount of actual or potential injury caused by the misconduct; and (4) the existence of any aggravating or mitigating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctioning is fact-specific and considers duty breached, mental state, injury, and aggravating/mitigating circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal timing, briefs, and compliance with appellate rules (§11.55(a)-(m),(o)-(p))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 14 days after the initial decision, either party may appeal to the USPTO Director by filing a notice of appeal (cross-appeal within 14 days after service of the notice of appeal). The appellant's brief shall be filed within 30 days after service of the record; appellee's brief within 30 days after service of appellant's brief; reply briefs within 14 days. Briefs must comply with specified Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure provisions (28(a)(2),(3),(5),(10), and 32(a)(4)-(7) and other referenced rules) unless otherwise ordered. Briefs must reference pages of the certified record. Appeals must include exceptions to hearing officer decisions and supporting reasons; any exception not raised is waived. Motions on appeal must be served on opposing party and filed with the USPTO Director, include a memorandum, comply with FRAP formatting rules, and include a good-faith conferral statement; response and reply deadlines are 21 and 14 days respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict compliance with appellate timing, formatting, and conferral requirements is required; failure to raise exceptions waives issues on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Director review authority and final decisions (§11.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director shall decide appeals and has authority to conduct a de novo review of the factual record, may affirm, reverse, modify, or remand. The final decision may dismiss a proceeding, reverse or modify the initial decision, reprimand, suspend, or exclude the practitioner, and may require compliance with § 11.58 for suspension/exclusion. The final decision may condition reinstatement on steps to correct or mitigate the conduct or to prevent recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director's review can be de novo; outcomes include disciplinary sanctions and conditions on reinstatement; final decisions are transmitted to OED Director and respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration/modification of USPTO Director decision (§11.56(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent or the OED Director may make a single request for reconsideration or modification of the USPTO Director's decision if filed within 20 days from the date of entry of the decision; the other party may respond within 14 days. No request will be granted unless based on newly discovered evidence or clear error of law or fact, and the requestor must demonstrate that newly discovered evidence could not have been discovered earlier by due diligence. Such a request stays the effective date of the disciplinary order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconsideration is narrowly limited to new evidence or clear error; the requirement that evidence could not have been discovered earlier is strict; filing a request stays the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review timing and service requirements (§11.57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of the final decision by the USPTO Director may be had by petition filed in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 32 within 30 days after the date of the final decision. The respondent must serve the USPTO Director with the petition in accordance with Rule 4 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and § 104.2 of this chapter. Except as provided in §11.56(c), an order for discipline in a final decision will not be stayed except on proof of exceptional circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing and proper service are essential for judicial review; stays of discipline are exceptional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance and reinstatement prerequisites for disciplined practitioners (§11.58(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An excluded or suspended practitioner will not be automatically reinstated at the end of the period; unless otherwise ordered, such practitioners must comply with §11.58 and §11.60 to be reinstated. A practitioner transferred to disability inactive status must comply with this section and §11.29. Failure to comply may constitute grounds for denying reinstatement and cause for further action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is conditional on compliance with the listed requirements and proof thereof; noncompliance can bar reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice prohibitions while excluded/suspended (§11.58(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any excluded or suspended practitioner, or practitioner transferred to disability inactive status, shall not engage in practice before the Office in patent, trademark, or other non-patent matters; shall not advertise or otherwise hold themself out as authorized or able to practice before the Office; and shall take all necessary steps to remove any advertisements or other representations suggesting authorization to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute prohibition on practicing or holding out to practice before the Office; affirmative obligation to remove representations implying authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thirty-day obligations after discipline order (§11.58(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days after the order date, an excluded or suspended practitioner must: (1) withdraw from representation in all matters pending before the Office; (2) provide written notice of the order to all State and Federal jurisdictions and administrative agencies where admitted; (3) provide to all clients with immediate or prospective business before the Office written notice of the order calling attention to lack of authority after the effective date and any urgent dates, deliver papers/property or schedule pickup and call attention to urgency, and return unearned fees/advanced costs not expended; (4) provide written notice of the order to all opposing parties in matters pending before the Office and provide a mailing address for each client who is a party; and (5) serve all notices by certified mail return receipt requested unless recipient is outside the U.S., in which case use a delivery service that provides delivery confirmation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed affirmative notification and withdrawal duties within 30 days, including protecting client property, refunding fees, and proofable methods of service for notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forty-five-day affidavit of compliance and required attachments (§11.58(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 45 days after the order, the practitioner shall file with the OED Director an affidavit of compliance certifying full compliance with the order, this section, and §11.116 for withdrawal from representation. Appended to the affidavit shall be: (1) copies of each form of notice and names/addresses of recipients and return receipts; (2) a schedule showing location, title, and account number of every account holding client/trust/fiduciary funds for practice before the Office; (3) a schedule and evidence showing disposition of all client and fiduciary funds; (4) a list of all jurisdictions of admission; and (5) a description of steps taken to remove advertisements or representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit requires documentary proof and detailed financial/account schedules; names/addresses of clients remain confidential unless ordered otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to update correspondence address (§11.58(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: An excluded or suspended practitioner, or practitioner transferred to disability inactive status, shall continue to file a statement in accordance with §11.11 regarding any change of residence or other address to which communications may thereafter be directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must keep contact information current even while suspended/excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition for winding up practice (§11.58(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise ordered by the USPTO Director, an excluded or suspended practitioner shall not engage in any practice before the Office. The USPTO Director may grant limited recognition for a period of no more than 30 days to conclude work on behalf of a client on matters pending before the Office. If work cannot be concluded, the practitioner shall so advise the client so the client may make other arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short, limited authorization may be granted solely to wind up pending matters; practitioner must notify client if work cannot be finished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention and proof of compliance requirement (§11.58(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: An excluded or suspended practitioner shall retain copies of all notices sent and maintain records of steps taken under this section. The practitioner shall provide proof of compliance as a condition precedent to the granting of any petition for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining evidence of compliance is mandatory for any reinstatement petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted paralegal work and supervision requirements (§11.58(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: An excluded or suspended practitioner may act as a paralegal for a supervising practitioner or perform other layperson services provided: (1) the practitioner is under the direct supervision of the supervising practitioner; (2) the practitioner is a salaried employee of the supervising practitioner, the supervising practitioner's law firm, or a client-employer who employs the supervising practitioner as a salaried employee; (3) the supervising practitioner assumes full professional responsibility to any client and the Office for any work performed by the practitioner; and (4) the practitioner does not (i) communicate directly with a client or prospective client regarding immediate or prospective Office business; (ii) render legal advice or legal services regarding Office matters; or (iii) meet in person (regardless of supervising practitioner's presence) with Office employees, clients, prospective clients, or witnesses regarding immediate or prospective Office business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict limits on what a disciplined practitioner may do while employed as a paralegal; supervising practitioner must assume full responsibility and prohibit direct client or Office communications and legal advice by the disciplined practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement after aiding another while suspended or excluded (§11.58(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: When an excluded or suspended practitioner acts as a paralegal or performs services under the permitted conditions, the practitioner shall not be reinstated unless: (1) the practitioner has filed an affidavit explaining in detail the precise nature of all paralegal or other services performed and shows by clear and convincing evidence compliance with this section and all USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct; and (2) the supervising practitioner has filed a written statement that they have read the affidavit, believe every statement to be true, and believe that the excluded or suspended practitioner has complied with paragraph (h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement requires proof by clear and convincing evidence and a supervising practitioner's attestation; both filings are required to consider reinstatement.
